skill.name: skill-auditor
skill.description: Audits Claude skill definitions for structure, content quality, and maintainability, then produces recommendations for improvement or decomposition.
skill.summary: Review skill definitions and receive clear quality recommendations.
skill.author: BarisSozen

security_audit.summary: All 16 static findings are false positives. The reported system-reconnaissance match is a local validation error message, and the remaining matches are Markdown backticks and fences rather than executable Ruby or shell code. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent was found in the reviewed files.

static_findings.snippet: List all skills in the `.claude/skills/` directory:
For each skill directory, verify it contains the required `SKILL.md` file.
- `description`: 50+ characters, specific about triggers, no placeholders
For automated fixes, use the audit script with `--fix` flag:
See `references/audit-criteria.md` for detailed scoring rubrics and decomposition guidelines.

content.value_statement: Skill definitions can become inconsistent, incomplete, or difficult to maintain. This skill checks their structure and quality, then provides focused recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Finds skill directories that contain a SKILL.md file.
Checks YAML frontmatter for name and description fields.
Checks for When to Use and Workflow sections.
Reports word counts, TODO placeholders, and empty resource directories.
Scores audited skills and lists validation errors and warnings.
Suggests decomposition when a skill has excessive size or complexity.
limitations: Audits local skill files only and does not assess runtime security.
Uses heuristic checks and cannot determine whether all guidance is correct.
Does not automatically repair skill files despite documentation that mentions a fix option.
Only discovers immediate child skill directories in the selected path.

use_cases.title: Validate a new skill before release
use_cases.description: Check frontmatter, required sections, placeholders, and resource directories before sharing a new skill.

use_cases.title: Review a team skill collection
use_cases.description: Run a consistent quality review across local skills and identify files that need attention.

use_cases.title: Plan skill decomposition
use_cases.description: Identify oversized or multi-purpose skills that may be clearer as focused sub-skills.

prompt_templates.title: Check one skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the skill in .claude/skills/my-skill. Summarize validation failures, warnings, and the highest priority improvements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one local skill

prompt_templates.title: Review all local skills
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit every skill under .claude/skills. Group the results by quality score and list the required fixes first.

prompt_templates.title: Assess structure and scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit .claude/skills/release-helper. Check its frontmatter, workflow, resources, and whether it should be split into sub-skills.

prompt_templates.title: Create an improvement plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the skills in .claude/skills and produce a prioritized improvement plan. Include evidence for each recommendation and separate required fixes from optional refinements.

output_examples.input: Review all skills and identify candidates for decomposition.
output: Reason: The skill has nine workflow steps and several distinct concerns.
Suggested action: Separate setup guidance from troubleshooting guidance.

best_practices: Run the audit before packaging or distributing a skill.
Review warnings manually because heuristics cannot judge all content quality.
Keep each skill focused on a clear user goal and move detailed material into references.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a high score as proof that instructions are technically correct.
Do not use the audit as a substitute for security testing of bundled scripts.
Do not ignore TODO and placeholder warnings before publishing a skill.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits local skill definitions for required structure, content quality signals, resource directories, and complexity indicators.

faq.question: Does it modify my skills?
faq.answer: The included Python script reports findings. Its current implementation does not provide an automatic fix action.

faq.question: Can it audit a single skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The script supports auditing a single skill path when used with its single-skill option.

faq.question: What causes a lower score?
faq.answer: Missing frontmatter, missing required fields or sections, TODO placeholders, oversized content, and empty resource directories reduce the score.

faq.question: Does it find security vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: No. It checks documentation and structure quality, not security vulnerabilities or unsafe runtime behavior.

faq.question: When should I split a skill?
faq.answer: Consider splitting a skill when it is very long, has many distinct sections, or combines several independent workflows.
